whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text: The hologram is like a lens. It takes the light, we capture the light that's reflected from the object, and record the way it was reflected off of the object, and then reconstruct the way that happens. So what we're doing is, in these masters, they're kind of like the photo negatives, and from them we can make the transfers. And these two pieces I'll show you, you can see it's hard to get this aligned a little bit, because we're holding them, we have to find the exact reference angle for these, illuminated by the laser at the same angle that the reference beam was. If I tip it off, it goes away. So you can see now that we have all angles of view recorded as though she was actually sitting there. This is exactly as though when it reflected off of her in making the hologram. I was exploring the idea of looking at the form, and I was looking at the form, and what I liked in this case is I wanted to and I like the echoing quality in the way the hands, because there's actually a space that's created by the three forms together. So in this case, it's not the form you see, but it's the space you see straight on the left and right. And so there's actually a space in the middle, and I accent that, or I talk about that, here if I go fast, you can begin to get a feel of that form. I like this hologram, and it was actually an accidental shot. We shot this hologram, and what I got fascinated with is, is, is, is, if we're getting to see that these are two figurative spaces or forms, that's literally the canyon of the three-dimensional space in between these figures that we're looking at.
